caption:
Making green hydrogen usually needs platinum or iridium. Both are rare, expensive, and mostly imported. Indian scientists just found a way around both.

Researchers at the Centre for Nano and Soft Matter Sciences in Bengaluru, an autonomous DST institute, built a device that splits water into hydrogen using only solar energy and organic materials - combining a naturally occurring amino acid with a light-absorbing organic molecule, completely metal-free. Standard electrolysis leans on iridium or platinum catalysts, both scarce and heavily import-dependent for India.

A fuel of the future, built without the metals everyone else is competing for - that's not just clean energy, that's supply chain independence.

Sources: Department of Science & Technology, POWER Magazine (2026)
